items.title: Karolina Strassmayer interviewed by Monk Rowe, May 25, 2023
items.q: INTERVIEWER mentions Karl Berger's quote; INTERVIEWEE responds to the concept but does not mention Karl Berger personally.

ctx.x: I guess we’re freeing ourselves from playing, from doing these things like playing rhythm, playing melody, playing harmony, in that certain way but we still use time, we still use rhythm and melody and harmony but just not in a preconceived way I guess. But when I play free music I always tend, I gravitate toward certain things. My ear just takes me there. I just, to me, when I play free music then I begin to knit, if you will, a series of changes that I don’t share with the others. They follow or they don’t…

Well Karl Berger surprised me when he said that playing free music is much more precise than not, than non-free he says. “I make my own parameters and it’s not free like people think — play whatever you want.” He was very adamant about the fact that this takes much more concentration than you would think and there are guidelines but they’re self-imposed.

That’s a nice way to say it. There are guidelines and they are self-imposed and people just don’t know what the guideline is going to be at that moment, that they’re shifting guidelines maybe and you don’t agree on them necessarily. Everybody can have their own or you go with the other person’s guideline or — it’s — I’ve played quite a lot of free music with David Friedman and Drori Mondiak, my husband, on drums. David Friedman on vibraphone. And we did a whole CD and we never said one word about the music but…
